spec.description:
Retrieve information about trades/fills. By default, the most recent trades are returned. Unless otherwise stated, costs, fees, prices, and volumes are specified with the precision for the asset pair (`pair_decimals` and `lot_decimals`), not the individual assets' precision (`decimals`).

**API Key Permissions Required:** `Orders and trades - Query closed orders & trades`

trades.description: Whether or not to include trades related to position in output.

start.description: Starting unix timestamp or trade tx ID of results (exclusive).

end.description: Ending unix timestamp or trade tx ID of results (inclusive).

without_count.description: If true, does not retrieve the count of matching trades. Request can be noticeably faster for users with many trades, as this avoids an extra database query.

consolidate_taker.description: Whether or not to consolidate trades by individual taker trades.

ledgers.description: Whether or not to include related ledger ids for a given trade. Setting this to true will slow request performance.

rebase_multiplier.description: Optional parameter for viewing xstocks data. `rebased` displays in terms of underlying equity, `base` displays in terms of SPV tokens.

pair.description: Filter results to a single trading pair. An unrecognized pair returns `EQuery:Unknown asset pair`.

limit.description: Number of trades returned per page. Values above 100 get clamped to 100.

response.title: TradeHistoryFrame
response.description: Wire frame; the generated method returns `result`.

error.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

count.description: Amount of available trades matching criteria. Omitted from the response when `without_count` is `true`.

ordertxid.description: Order responsible for execution of the trade.

postxid.description: Position responsible for execution of the trade.

price.description: Average price the order was executed at (quote currency).

cost.description: Total cost of the order (quote currency).

leverage.description: Amount of leverage used in the trade.

misc.description: Comma-delimited list of miscellaneous info: `closing` -- trade closes all or part of a position.

ledgers.description: List of ledger ids for entries associated with the trade (if requested).

trade_id.description: Unique identifier of the trade executed.

maker.description: `true` if the trade was executed with the user as the maker, `false` if taker.

aclass.description: Asset class of the traded pair.

tradeordertype.description: Order type of the trade (e.g. `market`, `limit`). May differ from `ordertype` when the order type was converted on execution.

posstatus.description: Position status. Only present if the trade opened a position.

cprice.description: Average price of the closed portion of the position (quote currency). Only present if the trade opened a position.

ccost.description: Total cost of the closed portion of the position (quote currency). Only present if the trade opened a position.

cfee.description: Total fee of the closed portion of the position (quote currency). Only present if the trade opened a position.

cvol.description: Total volume of the closed portion of the position (quote currency). Only present if the trade opened a position.

cmargin.description: Total margin freed in the closed portion of the position (quote currency). Only present if the trade opened a position.

net.description: Net profit/loss of the closed portion of the position (quote currency). Only present if the trade opened a position.

trades.description: List of closing trades for the position (if available). Only present if the trade opened a position.

notes: `HistoricalTrade.type` gets `enum: [buy, sell]` even though upstream's OpenAPI leaves it a bare string -- its own `description` documents the closed set ("Type of order (buy/sell)"), and rule 2 treats that as documented. `ordertype`/`tradeordertype` stay bare: their descriptions give examples (`market`, `limit`) rather than an exhaustive list. `posstatus` similarly gets `enum: [open, closed]` from its documented "Position status (open/closed)" description.

Request parameters are declared as `parameters`/`in: 'query'` here rather than as flat `requestBody` properties, unlike every sibling private endpoint in this client (S18 fix, production_standards.md): `typed_dev.codegen.python.Generator.paged_size_default` (shared, common/lib) only scans `operation.parameters` for a page-size parameter's declared `default`, and this endpoint's `limit` (default 50) needs that default found for `trades_history_paged` to generate at all -- `in: 'query'` states the parameter's role, not its literal wire placement (docs/spec/authoring.md rule 0), so this is spec-correct even though the wire request is still a form-urlencoded POST body via `authed_request`, unchanged. Deliberately narrow: many other private kraken endpoints declare a documented `default` on a `requestBody` parameter too (a stylistic pattern observed but not addressed here, since only this one endpoint's spec change was in scope for the S18 fix) -- if `trades_history`'s fix generalizes well, revisit whether the others should move too, as a separate, explicitly-scoped pass.

`paged_page1`/`paged_page2` examples are synthetic, not real captures -- built purely to exercise `trades_history_paged`'s multi-page walk against the mock server (production_standards.md S18), since the real account behind `default` has only a single real trade (below), not enough for a genuine multi-page series. Schema-valid, plausible-shaped `HistoricalTrade` rows, but the txids/prices/timestamps are invented, not venue-observed.

`time` is required: `default` now records one genuine trade (a real tiny XBTUSDC market buy, placed specifically to settle this field -- the account previously had zero real trade history, `count: 0, trades: {}`), and `time` is present on it, matching every other trade-record type in this client treating time as fundamental and the endpoint's own semantics ('the most recent trades are returned'). Also notable: this real trade's `leverage` is `"0"`, not the `"none"` seen on `closed_orders`' real capture -- confirms `leverage` genuinely mixes literal words and numbers across real responses and stays a bare `string`, not `decimal-string`.
